author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
Aldehyde dehydrogenase domain (IPR015590)

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Drosophila FBgn0036403/Q7KUK0

* **Description of issue**
IPR015590 is annotated with the high-level term 'oxidoreductase activity', but there is at least one protein in Drosophila that has this domain but lacks activity. There are more specific/useful GO terms on the children of IPR015590. Would you consider removing 'oxidoreductase activity' from IPR015590?
title: InterPro2GO issue: Aldehyde dehydrogenase domain (IPR015590)

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Steven,
Thank you very much. I have removed the term from this entry. The children have more specific terms added, for instance: IPR044148 has GO:0004030 - aldehyde dehydrogenase [NAD(P)+] activity, IPR000965 has GO:0004350 - glutamate-5-semialdehyde dehydrogenase (NADP+) activity, IPR005933 has GO:0003842 - L-glutamate gamma-semialdehyde dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity and in the case of IPR044086, I added GO:0004029 - aldehyde dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity and changed to type Family (removed the relationship with IPR015590). Let me know if I you agree with this.

Thanks!
Sara
